payload.body_markdown:
# FINDING: kosmos-oden modern-era connection verified end-to-end; Hermes 401 root-caused

## Scope
Owner-directed connectivity check 2026-09-29 on the kosmos-oden MCP server. Verifying the modern
MCP era (2026-07-28) still connects from three independent client paths, and diagnosing a live
Hermes-side connection failure.

## Server state (verified this pass, not recalled)
- `http://192.168.5.95:4816/mcp` responds; `server/discover` -> `supportedVersions: ["2026-07-28"]`,
  `capabilities: ["tools"]`, `serverInfo {name: kosmos-oden, version: 0.8.3}`.
- `tools/list` -> 18 tools, result keys `_meta, cacheScope, resultType, tools, ttlMs`. The previously
  filed cacheScope/ttlMs defect stays RESOLVED at v0.8.3; strict wire validation passes.
- Legacy `initialize` is still rejected with `-32602 params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]
  is required and must be a string`. Modern-only enforcement is unchanged and correct.

## Three-path verification (all pass)
1. Raw HTTP (stdlib probe, `_meta` envelope + Mcp-Method header): server/discover 200, tools/list 200, 18 tools.
2. Python SDK 2.0.0: `discover()` + `list_tools()` (18) + `call_tool("vault_overview")` + `search_notes` ->
   `is_error: false` on both.
3. Hermes native client: `hermes mcp test Kosmos-Oden` -> `Connected (1233ms)`, `Tools discovered: 18`;
   the live gateway then registered 18 `mcp__Kosmos_Oden__*` tools.

## Live vault read (vault_overview)
vault Obsidian-Oden, server 0.8.3, engine library 2.2.0 (bundled-package), gkxProfile 2.3,
readOnly true, sensitivityCeiling regulated, 2349 notes, 1838 GKX notes, 21 areas.
Note count moved 2257 -> 2349 since the 2026-09-12 reading.

## Root cause of the Hermes failure (client config, fixed)
`mcp_servers.Kosmos-Oden.headers.Authorization` held a masked/truncated literal ending `..teI4`
(a 20-character header value, not the 43-character token) and was not an env ref. Every attempt
returned HTTP 401 from Hermes, which is what parked the server at last startup. Fixed by setting the
header to `Bearer ${MCP_KOSMOS_ODEN_API_KEY}` and enabling the entry. No server-side change needed.

Config-shape note: `protocolVersion: 2026-07-28` is not a Hermes mcp_servers key. The working knob is
`protocol: stateless` (discover-first), which this entry now carries; Hermes injects the
`MCP-Protocol-Version` header itself when it is absent.

## Finding F-K1 (informational, client-side, no server action)
Hermes HEAD's era classifier `tools/mcp_tool_errors.py::_handshake_rejected_as_modern` recognizes
`-32022` and `-32601`/method-not-found, but NOT the `-32602` envelope-demand shape this server returns.
An entry left at `protocol: auto` therefore parks on `-32602 ... protocolVersion is required` instead of
retrying via `server/discover`. The one-line client fix is not in HEAD: commit `bbe22137` exists only in
`refs/hermes-update-backups/orphan-main-20260910-025933-bbe22137ae44` (the auto-updater resets divergent
local trees, so a local patch is not durable). Standing workaround, and the reason the fix is config-side
only: set `protocol: stateless` per server. Nothing to change on the kosmos-oden side.

## Duplicate entry
`mcp_servers.Kosmos-Oden-95` points at the same URL with the same token value under a second env var and
no `protocol` key; it is the entry that parks on `-32602`. It stays disabled. Recommend removing it, or
giving it `protocol: stateless` - two entries at one URL would double-register the 18 tools.

## Remaining gaps
- The 18 tools registered process-wide only after the fix; the session that requested this check had its
  tool schema assembled earlier, so native calls land from the next session onward.
- `-32602` classifier gap above stays open upstream until carried as a real PR.
